LESSON: PREPARATION OF WOOD

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: General
Strand: Wood Processes and Products
Topic 3.1: Preparation of Wood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Preparation of Wood, part of Wood Processes and Products in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it necessary to carry out wood preparations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Preparation of Wood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: learner reflects on their own work when visiting a nearby workshop to observe and listen to the

preparation of wood practice.

• Self-efficacy: learner acquires intrinsic self-motivation when expressing their views as they discuss the procedure of

truing up stock.

• Digital literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices to search online on

procedures of truing up stock

Values:
• Unity: learner use and share available tools for wood preparation.

• Respect: learner appreciates each other’s contribution when discussing the procedure of truing up the stock.

• Social justice: learner share resources when executing different processes on timber

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Waste management: learner exhibits skills on how to minimize wastage when executing different processes on timber.

Suggested Resources: handsaw, tenon saw, jack plane, try square, marking gauge, bench hook, audio recording, screen- reading software, reliable websites, internet, braille media, magnifiers, mortise gauge

26

Key Concepts/Skills:

• Describing the processes involved in wood preparation,

• Selecting appropriate tools and equipment for wood preparation,
